actions.justification: Mandatory first step - activating stroke team immediately to mobilize resources and ensure time-sensitive stroke protocol is initiated. This is the cornerstone of stroke care and enables parallel processing of all subsequent steps.
Mandatory - Last known well time is critical for determining tPA and thrombectomy eligibility windows (3-4.5h for tPA, up to 24h for thrombectomy in selected patients). Must be obtained immediately.
Mandatory - NIHSS score quantifies stroke severity, guides treatment decisions (tPA eligibility, thrombectomy candidacy), and establishes baseline neurological status for monitoring.
Mandatory: Hypoglycemia can mimic stroke and must be excluded immediately. Glucose check is critical in acute stroke assessment.
Mandatory: IV access is required for potential tPA administration and medication delivery in acute stroke management.
Mandatory: ECG is needed to identify atrial fibrillation or other arrhythmias that may be the cardioembolic source of stroke.

Mandatory lab workup for stroke assessment - CBC, BMP, and coagulation studies needed to evaluate for contraindications to thrombolysis and assess baseline hematologic/metabolic status. Must be completed within 60-minute deadline.

Mandatory STAT CT head required to differentiate ischemic from hemorrhagic stroke before any treatment decisions can be made. This is the critical imaging step in acute stroke workup and must be completed within 60-minute deadline.
Assess pre-stroke modified Rankin Scale to establish functional baseline, which is essential for determining eligibility for thrombolysis and/or thrombectomy and for informed consent discussions.

After CT head is obtained, the ASPECTS score should be assessed to evaluate the extent of early ischemic changes, which is critical for determining eligibility for reperfusion therapy in ischemic stroke.
Early activation of the neurointerventional team is essential if the patient is a candidate for mechanical thrombectomy, ensuring no delays if large vessel occlusion is identified on imaging.
Antiplatelet therapy assessment is relevant at this stage as part of the ischemic stroke workup, pending confirmation of stroke type and eligibility for thrombolytics.

Serial vital sign monitoring is essential for ongoing assessment of this stroke patient. Continuous monitoring helps detect hemodynamic instability, hypertension requiring management, or deterioration.
Blood pressure management is critical in acute stroke. Current BP is 120/80 which is within normal range, but ongoing monitoring and management protocols should be initiated per stroke guidelines.
Hyperglycemia worsens stroke outcomes. Glucose monitoring and management should be initiated as a standard supportive care measure in acute stroke care.

Hyperthermia (fever) worsens ischemic brain injury. Temperature monitoring and management protocols should be initiated per stroke guidelines. Current temp is 37.0°C but ongoing monitoring is indicated.

For potential thrombolysis candidate, BP must be maintained below 185/110 mmHg. Current BP 120/80 is acceptable but requires active monitoring and management protocol in place prior to tPA administration.
Patient requires admission to stroke unit or ICU for continuous monitoring, neurological checks, and further workup following acute stroke protocol.

Action order_stat_ct_head performed 10 min after deadline
